correctness.rationale: Every facet is one sign choice per antipodal edge pair because the star edge vectors are linearly independent. Its unique intrinsic normal is (S/n,S/n-epsilon_i), with squared length m-S^2/n. This yields an exact inradius upper bound from opposite extremal facets, attained at the origin. The spans of minimal-imbalance sign vectors have rank m for odd m and m-1 for even m, forcing respectively the zero center and the one-parameter center line. All remaining clearance inequalities reduce exactly to |S u| <= 1-sqrt(1-S^2/(mn)); the strictly increasing threshold in S proves the displayed endpoints and exact tangent-facet counts. Antipodal vertex averaging separately proves the unique radius-sqrt(2) outer sphere. An independent full-facet LP replay confirms small parameters but is not substituted for the all-m proof.

value.rationale: Stars are the canonical maximally branching trees; the primary graph-polytope literature shows that all tree symmetric-edge polytopes are unimodularly equivalent crosspolytopes, so their realized Euclidean differences carry genuinely new information beyond combinatorics. The result gives the full natural incenter invariant, not just a numerical formula, and discovers a strict leaf-parity phase change: the incenter locus alternates between a point and a segment with explicit nonzero length, while the segment endpoints acquire an exact additional facet-contact orbit. This is a substantive qualitative boundary in a fundamental graph-polytope family and is not a routine affine relabeling of known formulas.
